big_idea: Detectives use sort, frequency, graphs, mean+mode to TELL the data's story.
learning_intention: We are learning to analyse data and write a conclusion using mean and mode.
student_learning_goal: I can analyse data and write a conclusion using mean and mode.
success_criteria: I can BUILD a frequency table.
I can BUILD a scaled bar graph.
I can find MEAN and MODE.
I can WRITE a conclusion using both.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Detective Dot and Tally — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Detective Dot: Today's BIG CASE — survey, table, scale graph, mean, mode, conclude. The complete detective sweep! Dot + Tally open: 'Sort, TABLE, GRAPH, MEAN/MODE — case CLOSED!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Detective Dot and Tally puppets in capes. 'Friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We use ALL we know: tree diagrams, frequency tables, scaled graphs, mean, mode, and conclusions.'

Review the 5 detective steps: 'Step 1 — ASK + survey. Step 2 — FREQUENCY TABLE. Step 3 — SCALED bar graph. Step 4 — MEAN + MODE. Step 5 — CONCLUDE using both.'

Demo. 'Class survey: hours of TV per week.' Show 8 student responses: 5, 3, 8, 5, 10, 5, 2, 4.

Frequency table: 2(1), 3(1), 4(1), 5(3), 8(1), 10(1).
Mean: 42÷8 = 5.25 (round to 5).
Mode: 5 (appears 3 times).

Scaled bar graph: hours 0-10, scale 1=1 (small data, no scaling needed).

Conclusion: 'In our class, students watch about 5 hours of TV per week (mean). The mode is also 5 hours, the most common amount.'

'Detective Dot says — mean tells the AVERAGE, mode tells what's COMMON. Use BOTH in your conclusion.'

Now show the 5 stations:
- Station 1: TREE — sort 8 cards by 3 attributes.
- Station 2: FREQUENCY — build table from class survey.
- Station 3: SCALED GRAPH — build with 1 unit = 5.
- Station 4: MEAN + MODE — calculate for given data.
- Station 5: CONCLUDE — write using mean and mode.

Each child rotates and records on TEMPLATE.

'Detective Dot says — every BIG case ends with a CONCLUSION using mean AND mode.'

steps.instruction: Hand out templates. 5 stations rotation (~5 min each).
Stations 1-5: tree, frequency, scale, mean+mode, conclude.
Help with mean calculation as needed.

STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share their case analysis — Pair A focused on mode, Pair B on mean. Class debates: do both reach the same conclusion? When does each summary tool matter? Cite Konold & Pollatsek (2002) on data analysis tools.
steps.teacher_prompt: Dot: 'Same data, different tools, sometimes different stories. The DETECTIVE picks the right tool.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk between 5 stations physically. NO-PAPER VERSION: children rotate through 5 carpet zones (sort tree, frequency table, bar graph, mean/mode, conclusion). Body becomes the data flow.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: tree; frequency; scale; mean+mode; conclude.

discussion_prompts: What goes in a frequency table?
What's a CONCLUSION with mean and mode?
consolidation.exit_routine: Capstone refrain — Dot + Tally call: 'Sort, TABLE, GRAPH, MEAN/MODE — case CLOSED!' Class chants 3x. Each child shares their case + the tool they used at each step.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child writes a conclusion WITHOUT mean or mode — repairing the no-measure-conclusion trap at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the data-detectives capstone, the Grade-3 trap is single-tool fixation — child uses ONLY mode (Day 4) or only the bar graph (Day 3) instead of integrating all four prior-day tools (sort tree → frequency table → bar graph → mean/mode). Lehrer & Schauble (2002) place tool integration as the data-modelling terminal target.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4 into a peer case-investigation.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Capstone Station 5. Child writes 'Most students chose hockey.' No mean or mode mentioned.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Detective Dot asks — what's the MODE? What's the MEAN? Include those NUMBERS.'

Guide. 'Mode = hockey. Mean? If we numbered: 0 (none) to 5 (hockey is favourite) — mean would be the average.'

Generlise. 'Detective Dot says — at G3, conclusions use MODE (most common) AND MEAN (average) when possible.'

If still vague: provide a 'measures-required' frame. 'The mode is ___ (most common). The mean is ___ (average).'
expected_student_responses: (Stretched) Articulates difference between mean and mode.
common_misconceptions: Conclusion = group statement only. (Repair: G3 includes mean/mode.)
Mode and mean are the same. (Repair: different measures.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child names mode but not mean: model 'add all values, divide by count' on a 4-value set; child re-computes.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child uses only one tool: explicit checklist (sort, tabulate, graph, summarize); child checks all four before final report.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child analyses but skips conclusion: force the sentence frame 'The data shows ___ because mean = ___ and mode = ___.'

parts_outline.task: Build a frequency table from given survey data (8 students).
Build a scaled bar graph (1 unit = 2). Find mean and mode.
Write a conclusion using BOTH mean and mode.
